section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1984
title: 7 ## Causes of Accidental Deaths The total accidental deaths recorded during 1984 have been classified under two broad categories: (A) Accidental Deaths due to natural causes like lightning, heat strokes, floods, land slides, cold and exposure and cyclone and (B) Accidental deaths due to other causes like mishaps in factories, road accidents, air crashes, house collapse and boat capsizing etc. Category (A) accounted for 3·2 per cent of total accidental deaths recorded in 1984 in comparison to 3·5 per cent recorded in 1983. Under this category, the maximum number of deaths in 1984 were due to ‘Lightning’ (1,406) followed by ‘Floods’ (774) ‘Cyclone’ (691), ‘Land Slides’ (506), ‘Heat Strokes’ (503) and ‘Cold and Exposure’ (361). Category (B) claimed 96·8 per cent of the total accidental deaths registered during 1984 as against 96·5 per cent registered during 1983. Under this category the highest number of accidental deaths in 1984 was recorded under the head ‘Accidental Deaths on Roads’ (29,375) followed by ‘Drowning’ (22,729), ‘By Fire’ (15,741), ‘In Railways’ (12,735), ‘By Poisoning’ (6,735), ‘By Snake Biting’ (3,753), ‘By Fire Arms’ (1,796) ‘By Accidental Fall from Height’ (1,670) ‘By House Collapse’ (1,220), ‘By Accidental Electrocution by Appliances (1,160) and ‘By Animal Bitings’ (1,014). The remaining heads recorded the number of accidental deaths below 1,000. The Miscellaneous Causes recorded a total number of (29,659) accidental death cases during 1984, as against (33,069) cases in 1983 sharing 22·0 per cent of the total accidental deaths. During 1984 ‘Accidental deaths on Roads’ accounted for 21·8 per cent
